Hierarchical (mixed-effects) count regression

Source: R/countreg_hier.R
countreg_hier.Rd

Fits count models with normally distributed random effects at one or more grouping levels, nested or crossed, written as in lme4: (1 | site) for a random intercept, (1 + lnaadt | county) for correlated random intercepts and slopes, (1 | county/segment) for segments nested in counties and (1 | site) + (1 | year) for crossed effects. Any count family of countreg() can be used, including user-defined families, and the distribution parameters can depend on covariates.

Usage

countreg_hier(
  formula,
  data,
  family = "NB2",
  dis_param_formula_1 = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_2 = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  engine = c("auto", "aghq", "laplace", "msl"),
  nAGQ = NULL,
  re_dist = "normal",
  re_draws = 500,
  cre = NULL,
  cre_group = NULL,
  method = "BFGS",
  max.iters = 1000,
  start.vals = NULL,
  ndraws = 1500,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE,
  keep_data = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

a model formula with random-effect terms. The fixed part is as in countreg() (including offset()), and can have penalized smooth terms s() and t2() of mgcv. Group-level predictors are ordinary columns (constant within groups), and cross-level interactions are ordinary interactions.

data

a data frame.

family

a count family: a name from countreg()'s list, or a family made with new_count_family().

dis_param_formula_1, dis_param_formula_2

optional one-sided formulas for the family's distribution parameters.

offset

optional names of offset columns (or use offset() in the formula).

weights

optional frequency weights of the rows (a column name or a numeric vector).

engine

the approximation of the integral over the random effects: "aghq" (adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature; one grouping term only), "laplace" (any number of terms, nested or crossed, and smooth terms), "msl" (maximum simulated likelihood; one grouping term, any re_dist), or "auto" (simulation for non-normal effects, quadrature for a single grouping term with at most two effects, otherwise Laplace).

nAGQ

number of quadrature points per effect for "aghq" (default 9 for one effect, 5 for two or three). nAGQ = 1 is the Laplace approximation.

re_dist

distribution of the random effects of the grouping term: "normal" (default), "uniform", "triangular" (symmetric) or "gamma"; one value, or one per effect. Effects other than normal need a single grouping term and use engine = "msl". With "gamma" (one effect) the multiplicative group effect \(\exp(b_j)\) is gamma with mean 1 and standard deviation sd_..., as in the negative binomial random-effects model; with the others \(b_j\) has mean 0 and the reported standard deviation.

re_draws

number of (randomly shifted) Halton draws per group for engine = "msl".

cre

optional one-sided formula of time-varying regressors whose group means are added to the mean model (correlated random effects; see cre_test()).

cre_group

the grouping column(s) for the means of cre; by default those of the random-effect terms, when all terms share them.

method

optimizer for optim(): "BFGS" (default) or "Nelder-Mead".

max.iters

maximum number of optimizer iterations.

start.vals

optional starting values for the fixed coefficients and distribution parameters (as in countreg()), optionally followed by the random-effect standard deviations and correlations.

ndraws

number of Halton draws for families whose density is simulated (as in countreg()).

seed

seed of the random shifts of the Halton draws of engine = "msl".

verbose

print the optimizer's progress.

keep_data

keep the training data in the fit (needed for predictions without newdata).

Value

An object of class c("countreg_hier", "flexCountReg"). Methods: summary(), predict(), fitted(), residuals(), simulate(), fixef(), ranef(), VarCorr(), coef(), vcov(), logLik() and re_lrtest().

Details

The random effects of grouping term \(l\) are \(b_{lj} \sim N(0, \Sigma_l)\) for each of its groups \(j\), and enter the log of the mean: $$\log \mu_i = x_i'\beta + o_i + \sum_l z_{li}' b_{l, g_l(i)}.$$ Each \(\Sigma_l = L_l L_l'\) is estimated through its Cholesky factor with an unconstrained diagonal, so a variance can be estimated as zero (a singular fit, reported by summary()).

The marginal likelihood integrates the random effects out. With engine = "aghq" each group's integral uses Gauss-Hermite nodes centered at the group's mode and scaled by its curvature; this is accurate for small groups and is the default for one grouping factor. engine = "laplace" uses the Laplace approximation, as lme4::glmer() (with nAGQ = 1) and glmmTMB do, which handles crossed and nested terms with sparse matrices. The derivatives of the log-density are analytic for the Poisson, NB1 and NB2 families and numerical for the others.

Smooth terms are fitted in their mixed-model form: the penalized part of each smooth is a block of independent normal coefficients with variance \(1/\lambda\), so the smoothing parameters are estimated by the (Laplace) marginal likelihood, as in gamm4. Their coefficients are reported on mgcv's basis, with the covariance of the coefficients and effects given the variance parameters, so plot_smooths() and the other smooth tools work as for countreg().

With engine = "msl" the group likelihoods are averages over re_draws draws of each group's effects, so effects can have any of the re_dist distributions; the effects of the groups (ranef()) are then posterior means.

Standard errors come from the numerical Hessian of the marginal log-likelihood. The variance components are reported as standard deviations and correlations (sd_(Intercept)|site); their Wald standard errors are rough near zero, where the likelihood-ratio test of re_lrtest() is preferable.

countreg_rp() fits random parameters with a free mean and non-normal distributions at one level; renb() and repois() fit conjugate random effects in closed form.

See also

predict.countreg_hier(), ranef()

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
h <- countreg_hier(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + speed50 + offset(lnlength) +
                     (1 | ID), data = washington_roads, family = "NB2")
summary(h)
#> Hierarchical count model: NB2
#> Integration: adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, 9 points
#> Call: countreg_hier(formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + speed50 + offset(lnlength) + (1 | ID), data = washington_roads, family = "NB2")
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>  Groups Name        Variance Std.Dev.
#>  ID     (Intercept) 0.408    0.6388  
#> Number of obs: 1501; groups: ID, 507
#> 
#> Fixed coefficients and distribution parameters:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept) -9.00121    0.50404 -17.858  < 2e-16 ***
#> lnaadt       1.11659    0.05893  18.948  < 2e-16 ***
#> speed50     -0.57519    0.13021  -4.417 9.99e-06 ***
#> ln(alpha)   -6.80660   47.40990  -0.144    0.886    
#> 
#> Random-effect standard deviations and correlations (Wald SEs):
#>                   Estimate Std. Error
#> sd_(Intercept)|ID   0.6388    0.06618
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -1069.365   AIC: 2148.73   BIC: 2175.30
VarCorr(h)
